verdictStatement: Eight of the nine claimed repairs land, several exactly as the frozen findings specified, and the custody frame that produced Codex's blocker is now clean on both sides: the prompt supplies the authorization that was missing, and reMeasurementAtV12 republishes a pin that reproduces byte-for-byte at the dispatched HEAD. tcbCarrier finally admits verifiedInstallRoot with a kind, an author, a ceremony and an existence rule tied to dependencyIfCarrierAbsent, and bindingPoint is amended to exclude it explicitly — my CLAUDE-V11-S1 in full. starttime is re-cited as the twenty-second whitespace-separated field after the final ')' in both places, with the same prohibition sentence the mountinfo token carries, and the token 'field 22' no longer occurs. The Linux namespace inode is now read before and after the mountinfo observation bound to the same {pid, starttime} pair, closing the setns race Codex found. NFC-then-UTF-8 is restored and ordered before grammar validation and signing, with equality defined on UTF-8 bytes after NFC. The ledger narrative repairs all landed. What holds acceptance is that the closed-schema repair was added beside the old representation rather than reconciled with it: preselectionRecord declares kind 'preselection', which the unchanged closed eventKind enumeration does not admit; retainedEventSchema and evidenceJoin are byte-identical to v11, so the flat per-event labels and the undefined PreselectionFilesystemObservation both survive alongside the new records and the new volumeEquality join.

shouldFix.title: The new closed volume schema was added beside the old one: 'preselection' is not an admitted eventKind, and retainedEventSchema and evidenceJoin are unchanged, so two parallel representations and two join rules coexist
shouldFix.location: /loaderTraces/preselectionRecord/kind, /loaderTraces/laterEventVolumeFields and /loaderTraces/volumeEquality, read against the unchanged /loaderTraces/retainedEventSchema and /loaderTraces/evidenceJoin

measurement.eventKindNotAdmitted: preselectionRecord declares kind 'preselection'. retainedEventSchema is byte-identical to v11 and still states the closed enumeration 'eventKind (resolution-attempt|use|refusal|inapplicable)'. A producer emitting a preselection record must therefore set eventKind to a value outside the enumeration, or cannot emit the record conformingly. Codex's PTCB-V11-S2 requiredRepair offered 'a closed qualification-run record or explicit preselection event kind'; v12 took the event-kind branch without widening the enumeration that closes it.
measurement.duplicateRepresentation: retainedEventSchema still carries the v10/v11 flat labels preselectionCanonicalVerifiedRoot, preselectionVolumeIdentity, preselectionFilesystemTypeToken, observedVolumeIdentity, observedFilesystemTypeToken and linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity. preselectionRecord and laterEventVolumeFields now define the same data under different names — canonicalVerifiedRoot, volumeIdentity, filesystemTypeToken. Nothing says which naming a producer emits, or that one supersedes the other.
measurement.undefinedNameSurvives: evidenceJoin is byte-identical to v11 and still reads 'PreselectionFilesystemObservation (canonicalVerifiedRoot, OS-tagged volume identity, filesystem-type token) MUST equal later observedVolumeIdentity and observedFilesystemTypeToken.' PTCB-V11-S2's second evidence bullet was precisely that this object 'appears only in evidenceJoin and is not defined as an object anywhere'. v12 defines preselectionRecord, which is a different name with a different field list, and leaves the sentence naming the undefined object in place.
measurement.twoJoinRules: volumeEquality now states the join in closed terms — 'Refuse unless later observedVolumeIdentity equals preselection volumeIdentity AND later observedFilesystemTypeToken equals preselection filesystemTypeToken. On Linux also refuse if linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity differs from the preselection pair (retargeting).' That is the correct rule. It now sits alongside the older overlapping sentence in evidenceJoin rather than replacing it.

shouldFix.whatLanded: Recorded in fairness, because the substance of PTCB-V11-S2 did land. preselectionRecord and laterEventVolumeFields are genuinely closed: each has requiredFields, linuxAlsoRequires and macosForbids, so mountNamespaceIdentity and linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity are required on Linux and forbidden on macOS in both records. volumeEquality supplies per-field equality and explicit refusal, and states that the OS-tagged serializations are the closed forms above. The gap is reconciliation, not design.
shouldFix.consequence: Two conforming producers can emit different field names for the same observation, and a verifier reading evidenceJoin looks for an object the artifact does not define while a second, differently-named rule states the same join. The retained evidence is no longer under-specified, but it is no longer singular either — and a preselection record cannot carry a lawful eventKind at all.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add 'preselection' to the eventKind enumeration in retainedEventSchema, or say that a preselectionRecord is a run record rather than an event and needs no eventKind. Retire the six flat preselection/observed labels in favour of preselectionRecord and laterEventVolumeFields, or state that the labels are those records' fields under their record names. Replace evidenceJoin's PreselectionFilesystemObservation sentence with a pointer to volumeEquality. Roster /loaderTraces again for that edit.
